spotlight.title: Cyber cafés and the IT jobs boom
spotlight.standfirst: In 1999 the web was something most people reached by the hour in a café, and the software industry that served the world's Y2K work was multiplying its exports.

items.title: Software exports
items.summary: India's software exports grew from 734 million US dollars in 1995 to 3.9 billion US dollars in 1999-2000, NASSCOM's figure, from 2.65 billion the year before.

sources.label: IndiaMart: article on the Indian software industry (27 November 2000)

items.title: How much was Y2K work
items.summary: One source puts Y2K contracts at 560 million US dollars, 21.1 percent of exports, in the prior year; another has NASSCOM putting Y2K at about 12 percent of software revenue in 1999-2000, and NASSCOM expected the work to fall off after 1999.

items.title: A small share of the economy
items.summary: The IT sector's share of India's exports was under 4 percent in FY1998, and its contribution to GDP was 1.2 percent in 1998; Chennai's TIDEL Park was the largest IT park in Asia when it opened in 1999.

items.title: An hour at the café
items.summary: In late 1999 an hour of surfing cost roughly Rs 30 to 60 in Bangalore and Chennai and Rs 10 to 30 in Hyderabad.

sources.label: Voice&Data: Andhra Pradesh, from tea cafes to cyber cafes

items.originalUnits: Rs 30-60 an hour in Bangalore and Chennai; Rs 10-30 in Hyderabad

items.title: 190 cafés in Hyderabad
items.summary: Hyderabad had about 190 cyber cafés by the end of November 1999, more than Bangalore or Chennai.

sources.label: Voice&Data: Andhra Pradesh, from tea cafes to cyber cafes

items.title: The first café
items.summary: The first Indian internet café is described as opening in July 1996 at a Mumbai hotel, charging Rs 800 for an hour.

sources.label: I Want To Know: The fascinating history of the internet in India

items.title: Few users
items.summary: India had just over 30,000 internet users in 1997 and about 50,000 connections in early 1998, and dial-up tariffs were falling to as low as Rs 20 an hour from January 1998.
